# Study design and data contracts

```{r}
source("R/figures.R")
```

## Cohorts and ascertainment

The historical conventional-testing cohort and the ONT report cohort are different
patient groups in the currently available tables. Both datasets contain selectively
reported clinically relevant findings rather than a complete inventory of all
variation detected by each assay. Consequently, their comparison estimates
differences in the **reported diagnostic spectrum**, conditional on referral,
calendar period, test menu and reporting policy. It is not a same-patient platform
accuracy analysis.

## Units of observation

Define and count unique people, specimens, analysis episodes and reports. Document
repeat testing, family relationships, referral pathway, assay version and what a
negative report means in each era.

## Provenance-preserving data model

Use the normalized episode, finding and phenotype tables generated by
`normalise_cohort_reports.py`. Preserve raw report wording beside every canonical
variant or haplotype interpretation. Blank cells remain `not_reported`; an explicit
sentinel remains `not_tested`.

## Missingness and analysis eligibility

Create a table listing each outcome, genotype field, covariate, unit, date relation
and eligible sample count. Do not use “clinical severity” unless a genuine severity
outcome is available.
